UR-1.t: Describe the sequence of pronephros, mesonephros, and metanephros, and identify the metanephros, appearing in the fifth week, as the source of the permanent kidney.

Explain how reciprocal induction between the ureteric bud and the metanephric mesenchyme forms the collecting system (collecting ducts, calyces, pelvis, ureter) and the nephron (Bowman capsule to distal convoluted tubule), and predict renal agenesis when induction fails.
Describe the ascent of the kidneys from the pelvis to the lumbar region, and explain how fusion of the lower poles produces a horseshoe kidney trapped beneath the inferior mesenteric artery.
Explain how early splitting of the ureteric bud or formation of two buds produces a bifid or duplex ureter, and relate an ectopic ureteral orifice to obstruction or reflux.

Trace partition of the cloaca by the urorectal septum into the urogenital sinus and anorectal canal, and predict a patent urachus (urine draining from the umbilicus) or urachal cyst from failed allantois obliteration.
Explain how posterior urethral valves in male infants obstruct urine outflow, and predict bilateral hydronephrosis, a distended bladder, and oligohydramnios.
UR-1.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders

UR-2.t: Describe the three layers of the glomerular filtration barrier (fenestrated endothelium, basement membrane with type IV collagen and negatively charged heparan sulfate, podocyte foot processes with slit diaphragms) and predict albuminuria when charge or foot processes are lost.
UR-2.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease

UR-2.t: Identify the components of the juxtaglomerular apparatus (renin-secreting juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole, macula densa of the distal thick ascending limb, extraglomerular mesangial cells) and the supporting and phagocytic roles of intraglomerular mesangial cells.

Distinguish proximal tubule (cuboidal cells with brush border and abundant mitochondria), thin limb (simple squamous), distal tubule (cuboidal without brush border), and collecting duct (principal and intercalated cells) epithelium, and relate high proximal tubule energy demand to ischemic injury.
Distinguish cortical from juxtamedullary nephrons by glomerulus position, loop of Henle length, and vasa recta supply, and relate long loops to urine concentrating ability.

Describe urothelium (transitional epithelium with umbrella cells), the lamina propria, and the detrusor muscle, and explain how the urothelium stretches during bladder filling while remaining impermeable to urine.

UR-3.t: Locate the kidneys in the retroperitoneum from about T12 to L3, explain why the right kidney lies lower than the left, and identify posterior relations (diaphragm, 12th rib, psoas major, quadratus lumborum).
Identify the anterior relations of the right kidney (liver, descending duodenum, right colic flexure) and left kidney (stomach, spleen, pancreatic tail, jejunum, left colic flexure).
Describe the renal coverings (fibrous capsule, perirenal fat, renal fascia, pararenal fat) and the anterior to posterior order of hilar structures (renal vein, renal artery, renal pelvis).

Trace the ureter along the psoas, across the iliac vessels at the pelvic brim, into the bladder wall, and predict that stones lodge at the ureteropelvic junction, pelvic brim, and ureterovesical junction.
UR-3.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: renal and ureteral calculi

UR-3.t: Describe the bladder trigone, the ureteric and internal urethral orifices, and the male urethral segments (prostatic, membranous, spongy), and contrast them with the short female urethra and its higher risk of ascending infection.
Predict the site of male urethral injury from a pelvic fracture (posterior urethra at the membranous segment) versus a straddle injury (bulbous part of the spongy urethra).
UR-3.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders

UR-4.t: Distinguish the retroperitoneal kidneys and ureters from the extraperitoneal bladder, and explain why dome rupture of a full bladder leaks urine into the peritoneal cavity while pelvic fracture causes extraperitoneal extravasation.
UR-4.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: bladder rupture

UR-4.t: Describe the peritoneal reflections over the bladder, including the rectovesical pouch in males and the vesicouterine and rectouterine pouches in females.
Explain why ureteral colic radiates from the flank to the groin, relating the pain to visceral afferents that enter the lower thoracic and upper lumbar spinal cord.
UR-4.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: renal and ureteral calculi

UR-4.t: Relate the posterior position of the kidney against the 12th rib and posterior abdominal wall to costovertebral angle tenderness in pyelonephritis and to the spread of a perinephric abscess within the renal fascia.
UR-4.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: upper urinary tract

UR-4.t: Explain why the ureter is at risk during hysterectomy, where it passes beneath the uterine artery near the cervix, and predict hydronephrosis or urine leak after ligation or transection.
UR-4.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: ureteral injury

UR-4.t: Relate pelvic floor and urethral support to stress incontinence and cystocele, and distinguish stress, urge (detrusor overactivity), and overflow incontinence by mechanism.
UR-4.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: urinary incontinence

UR-5.t: Trace renal blood flow from the renal artery through segmental, interlobar, arcuate, and cortical radiate arteries, afferent arteriole, glomerulus, efferent arteriole, and peritubular capillaries or vasa recta to the renal vein.
Explain why segmental and interlobar arteries behave as end arteries, and predict a wedge-shaped cortical infarct after embolic occlusion.
UR-5.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Vascular disorders: renal infarction

UR-5.t: Predict how afferent versus efferent arteriolar constriction or dilation changes renal plasma flow, GFR, and filtration fraction.
Explain renal autoregulation of blood flow and GFR by the myogenic response and tubuloglomerular feedback through the macula densa.
Explain how slow vasa recta flow and its countercurrent arrangement preserve medullary hypertonicity, and relate the low medullary oxygen tension to papillary necrosis and sickling in the vasa recta.
UR-5.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: tubulointerstitial disease: papillary necrosis

UR-5.t: Describe the course of the left renal vein between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery and its gonadal tributary, and predict a left varicocele when renal cell carcinoma invades the left renal vein.

UR-6.t: Explain how glomerular capillary hydrostatic and oncotic pressures and Bowman space pressure set GFR, and predict the GFR change with ureteral obstruction, hypoalbuminemia, and dehydration.

Calculate clearance (urine concentration times urine flow divided by plasma concentration), GFR from inulin or creatinine, effective renal plasma flow from PAH, and filtration fraction, and interpret clearance above or below GFR as net secretion or reabsorption.

Describe proximal tubule reabsorption (about two thirds of filtered sodium and water, nearly all glucose and amino acids, Na+/H+ exchange) and thick ascending limb transport (Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransport, water impermeability, paracellular Mg2+ and Ca2+ reabsorption).
Explain how aldosterone acts on principal cells (ENaC, Na+/K+-ATPase, K+ secretion), ADH inserts aquaporin-2 in the collecting duct, and PTH increases distal tubule calcium reabsorption.
UR-6.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: fluid volume and electrolyte/ion disorders

UR-6.t: Explain countercurrent multiplication and ADH-dependent urine concentration, and distinguish central diabetes insipidus, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, SIADH, and primary polydipsia by serum sodium, urine osmolality, and response to water deprivation and desmopressin.
UR-6.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: fluid volume and electrolyte/ion disorders: hyponatremia, hypernatremia

UR-6.t: Predict changes in extracellular and intracellular fluid volume and osmolality after isotonic, hypotonic, and hypertonic fluid gain or loss, and apply them to dehydration, hypovolemia, and volume overload.
UR-6.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: fluid volume and electrolyte/ion disorders: dehydration, hypovolemia, volume overload

UR-6.t: Describe the micturition reflex (pelvic parasympathetic detrusor contraction, sympathetic and pudendal sphincter control, pontine micturition center), and predict a reflex spastic bladder above the sacral cord versus a flaccid overflow bladder at the sacral cord.
UR-6.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: neurogenic bladder

UR-7.t: Explain how the proximal tubule reclaims filtered bicarbonate using carbonic anhydrase and Na+/H+ exchange, and how the kidney generates new bicarbonate by excreting H+ as titratable acid (mainly phosphate) and as ammonium made from glutamine in the proximal tubule.
UR-7.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: acid-base disorders

UR-7.t: Interpret arterial blood gases to classify metabolic and respiratory acidosis and alkalosis, judge compensation (Winters formula, acute versus chronic renal compensation), and identify mixed disturbances.
UR-7.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: acid-base disorders

UR-7.t: Calculate the anion gap and distinguish high anion gap metabolic acidosis (lactic acidosis, ketoacidosis, uremia, methanol, ethylene glycol, salicylates) from normal anion gap acidosis (diarrhea, renal tubular acidosis).
UR-7.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: acid-base disorders

UR-7.t: Distinguish renal tubular acidosis type 1 (distal, urine pH above 5.5, hypokalemia, calcium phosphate stones), type 2 (proximal bicarbonate wasting, hypokalemia, Fanconi syndrome), and type 4 (hypoaldosteronism, hyperkalemia).
UR-7.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: renal tubular acidosis

UR-7.t: Explain how vomiting causes hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia, and why volume depletion and aldosterone maintain it and produce paradoxical aciduria.
UR-7.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: acid-base disorders

UR-7.t: Trace renin release (low perfusion pressure at juxtaglomerular cells, low NaCl at the macula densa, beta-1 sympathetic input) through angiotensin II and aldosterone actions, and contrast the opposing effects of atrial natriuretic peptide.
Explain pressure natriuresis as the kidney's long-term control of arterial pressure, and predict hypertension with hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and low renin in primary hyperaldosteronism.
UR-7.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: hypertensive renal disease

UR-8.t: Explain sodium-coupled (SGLT2) glucose reabsorption in the proximal tubule with a transport maximum, and predict glucosuria and osmotic diuresis when plasma glucose exceeds the renal threshold (about 200 mg/dL) in diabetes mellitus.
Distinguish glomerular proteinuria (albumin), overflow proteinuria (Bence Jones light chains), and tubular proteinuria (failed proximal reabsorption of small filtered proteins).
UR-8.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Abnormalities of urine/urination: proteinuria

UR-8.t: Describe PTH and low phosphate stimulation of vitamin D 1-alpha-hydroxylation in the proximal tubule, predict serum calcium, phosphate, and PTH in chronic kidney disease, primary hyperparathyroidism, and vitamin D deficiency, and explain refractory hypocalcemia in hypomagnesemia.
UR-8.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: fluid volume and electrolyte/ion disorders: calcium, phosphate, magnesium disorders

UR-8.t: Explain potassium shifts into cells (insulin, beta-adrenergic stimulation, alkalosis) and out of cells (acidosis, cell lysis, insulin deficiency, hyperosmolality), and predict ECG findings of hyperkalemia (peaked T waves, wide QRS) and hypokalemia (U waves).
UR-8.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: fluid volume and electrolyte/ion disorders: hypokalemia, hyperkalemia

UR-8.t: Describe erythropoietin release by renal peritubular interstitial cells in response to hypoxia, and relate it to normocytic anemia in chronic kidney disease and secondary polycythemia in renal cell carcinoma.
UR-8.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: chronic kidney disease

UR-8.t: Explain how NAD+-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase starts the conversion of ethylene glycol to glycolic and oxalic acids, producing high anion gap metabolic acidosis, an osmolal gap, calcium oxalate crystals in urine, and acute tubular injury.
UR-8.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Toxins and environmental extremes: other chemical agents: ethylene glycol

UR-8.t: Explain the hyperlipidemia of nephrotic syndrome (increased hepatic lipoprotein synthesis and reduced lipoprotein catabolism) and identify lipiduria as oval fat bodies and fatty casts showing Maltese cross birefringence under polarized light.
UR-8.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: nephrotic syndrome

UR-9.t: Explain how autosomal dominant PKD1 (polycystin-1, chromosome 16) and PKD2 (polycystin-2, chromosome 4) mutations and autosomal recessive PKHD1 (fibrocystin) mutations cause polycystic kidney disease, and predict inheritance in a pedigree.
UR-9.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: benign neoplasms and cysts

UR-9.t: Explain how mutations in the alpha-3, alpha-4, or alpha-5 chains of type IV collagen (most often X-linked COL4A5) cause Alport syndrome, and how heterozygous COL4A3 or COL4A4 mutations cause thin basement membrane disease.
UR-9.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease

UR-9.t: Explain two-hit loss of the VHL tumor suppressor on chromosome 3p, with HIF stabilization driving VEGF expression, in sporadic clear cell renal carcinoma and von Hippel-Lindau syndrome (bilateral renal carcinoma, hemangioblastomas, pheochromocytoma).
UR-9.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: tumors linked to hereditary conditions

UR-9.t: Relate WT1 loss on chromosome 11p13 to Wilms tumor in WAGR and Denys-Drash syndromes, and 11p15 imprinting defects to Wilms tumor in Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome.
UR-9.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: tumors linked to hereditary conditions

UR-9.t: Explain how TSC1 or TSC2 mutations in tuberous sclerosis remove hamartin and tuberin inhibition of mTOR growth signaling, and relate this to renal angiomyolipomas (blood vessels, smooth muscle, fat) and renal cysts.
UR-9.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: tumors linked to hereditary conditions

UR-9.t: Explain how an autosomal recessive defect in the proximal tubule transporter for cystine, ornithine, lysine, and arginine causes cystinuria with hexagonal cystine stones and a positive cyanide-nitroprusside test.
UR-9.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: cystinuria

UR-9.t: Explain how X-linked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency in Fabry disease causes globotriaosylceramide accumulation, with angiokeratomas, painful neuropathy, hypohidrosis, and progressive renal failure.
UR-9.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: enzymatic/metabolic: Fabry disease

UR-10.t: Classify glomerular injury as type II hypersensitivity (anti-GBM antibodies to the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen, linear IgG, with lung hemorrhage in Goodpasture syndrome), type III immune complex disease (granular deposits), or pauci-immune ANCA disease, and name an example of each.
UR-10.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease

UR-10.t: Interpret serum complement in glomerular disease: low C3 in poststreptococcal and membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, low C3 and C4 in lupus nephritis, and normal levels in IgA nephropathy, anti-GBM disease, and ANCA vasculitis.
UR-10.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease

UR-10.t: Distinguish granulomatosis with polyangiitis (PR3-ANCA, necrotizing granulomas of the upper and lower airways, glomerulonephritis) from microscopic polyangiitis (MPO-ANCA, no granulomas), and contrast polyarteritis nodosa, which spares glomeruli and causes renal artery microaneurysms.
UR-10.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: polyangiitis, polyarteritis nodosa

UR-10.t: Describe IgA vasculitis in children (IgA immune complex deposition after an upper respiratory infection, palpable purpura on the buttocks and legs, arthralgia, abdominal pain, intussusception) and its mesangial IgA glomerulonephritis.
UR-10.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: IgA vasculitis

UR-10.t: Describe urinary tract defenses (one-way urine flow, complete bladder emptying, the flap-valve ureterovesical junction, urothelial shedding) and predict how obstruction, reflux, catheters, and pregnancy increase infection risk.
UR-10.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: lower urinary tract

UR-10.t: Explain how CD8+ T cells recognize renal cell carcinoma antigens on MHC class I and NK cells kill tumor cells that lose MHC class I, and how tumors evade immunity through PD-L1 expression and MHC class I downregulation.

Explain how the recombinant hepatitis B surface antigen vaccine induces protective anti-HBs antibodies, interpret anti-HBs alone as vaccine immunity, and relate vaccination to prevention of hepatitis B associated membranous nephropathy.

UR-11.t: Describe uropathogenic Escherichia coli (gram-negative lactose-fermenting rod from fecal flora) as the most common urinary pathogen, and relate type 1 fimbriae to cystitis and P fimbriae to pyelonephritis.

Identify Staphylococcus saprophyticus (coagulase-negative, novobiocin-resistant, young sexually active women), Klebsiella (mucoid capsule), Enterococcus, and Pseudomonas (catheter-associated) as other urinary pathogens.

Explain how Proteus mirabilis urease splits urea to ammonia, raising urine pH and precipitating magnesium ammonium phosphate (struvite) staghorn calculi, and relate swarming motility to its identification.
UR-11.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: renal and ureteral calculi

UR-11.t: Interpret urine dipstick and microscopy in infection: leukocyte esterase for pyuria, nitrite from Enterobacterales nitrate reductase, WBC casts for kidney involvement, and sterile pyuria suggesting urethritis or renal tuberculosis.

Compare Neisseria gonorrhoeae (gram-negative diplococcus, pili with antigenic variation, IgA protease) and Chlamydia trachomatis serovars D to K (obligate intracellular, elementary and reticulate bodies) as causes of urethritis, and identify nucleic acid amplification as the diagnostic test.
UR-11.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: lower urinary tract: chlamydial and nonchlamydial

UR-11.t: Relate infections to glomerular disease: nephritogenic group A streptococci to poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, hepatitis B to membranous nephropathy, hepatitis C to membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis with cryoglobulinemia, and HIV to collapsing FSGS.
UR-11.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: hepatitis B/C-related glomerular disease

UR-11.t: Describe hematogenous renal tuberculosis with caseating granulomas and sterile pyuria, and the Schistosoma haematobium life cycle (snail host, skin-penetrating cercariae, adults in vesical venules, terminal-spined eggs) leading to hematuria and bladder squamous cell carcinoma.
UR-11.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: upper urinary tract: renal tuberculosis

UR-12-A.t: Distinguish nephritic syndrome (hematuria with RBC casts, hypertension, oliguria, azotemia, proteinuria under 3.5 g/day) from nephrotic syndrome (proteinuria over 3.5 g/day, hypoalbuminemia, edema, hyperlipidemia, fatty casts).
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: nephrotic syndrome

UR-12-A.t: Interpret urinary findings to localize disease: RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs (glomerulonephritis), WBC casts (pyelonephritis, interstitial nephritis), muddy brown granular casts (acute tubular necrosis), fatty casts (nephrotic syndrome), and waxy casts (chronic kidney disease).
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Abnormalities of urine/urination: hematuria, proteinuria

UR-12-A.t: Describe poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis: onset weeks after streptococcal pharyngitis or impetigo, cola-colored urine, periorbital edema, hypertension, low C3, granular IgG and C3 deposits, and subepithelial humps on electron microscopy.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis

UR-12-A.t: Distinguish IgA nephropathy (episodic gross hematuria within days of a mucosal infection, mesangial IgA deposits) from poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis by timing of hematuria after infection and complement level.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: IgA nephropathy

UR-12-A.t: Classify rapidly progressive (crescentic) glomerulonephritis by immunofluorescence into anti-GBM (linear), immune complex (granular), and pauci-immune (ANCA) types, and identify crescents of fibrin, parietal epithelial cells, and macrophages.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease

UR-12-A.t: Describe lupus nephritis, with diffuse proliferative disease (subendothelial wire-loop deposits, nephritic picture) as the most common and most severe class and membranous disease causing nephrotic syndrome, and interpret low complement and anti-dsDNA antibodies.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: lupus nephritis

UR-12-A.t: Describe membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (mesangial proliferation, tram-track basement membrane duplication), with immune complex disease linked to hepatitis B and C and dense deposit disease (a C3 glomerulopathy) linked to C3 nephritic factor.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: hepatitis B/C-related glomerular disease

UR-12-A.t: Explain diabetic nephropathy: hyperfiltration, nonenzymatic glycation, and hyaline arteriolosclerosis of afferent and efferent arterioles lead to basement membrane thickening and mesangial expansion with Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules, progressing from microalbuminuria to nephrotic proteinuria and renal failure.

Describe focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (segmental sclerosis with podocyte injury and poor steroid response) and its secondary causes (HIV, heroin use, sickle cell disease, obesity), including the collapsing variant of HIV-associated nephropathy.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: tubulointerstitial disease: HIV nephropathy

UR-12-A.t: Explain the consequences of nephrotic syndrome: edema from hypoalbuminemia, hyperlipidemia from increased hepatic lipoprotein synthesis, hypercoagulability from urinary antithrombin III loss (renal vein thrombosis), and infection from immunoglobulin loss.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: nephrotic syndrome

UR-12-A.t: Describe minimal change disease in children: selective albuminuria, normal light microscopy and immunofluorescence, podocyte foot process effacement on electron microscopy, excellent corticosteroid response, and association with Hodgkin lymphoma.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: minimal change disease

UR-12-A.t: Describe membranous nephropathy in adults: subepithelial immune deposits with spike and dome basement membrane, anti-PLA2R antibodies in primary disease, and secondary causes (lupus, hepatitis B, solid tumors, drugs such as NSAIDs).
UR-12-A.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Neoplasms and related disorders: paraneoplastic syndromes: membranous glomerulonephritis

UR-12-A.t: Explain how amyloid deposition in glomeruli causes nephrotic syndrome, and identify AL (light chain) and AA (chronic inflammation) amyloid by apple-green birefringence with Congo red stain under polarized light.
UR-12-A.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: structural protein disorders: amyloidosis

UR-12-A.t: Classify acute kidney injury as prerenal, intrinsic, or postrenal, and interpret BUN to creatinine ratio (over 20 prerenal), fractional excretion of sodium (under 1 percent prerenal, over 2 percent tubular necrosis), and urine osmolality.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: acute kidney injury

UR-12-A.t: Identify diabetes and hypertension as the leading causes of chronic kidney disease, and predict its consequences: uremia (pericarditis, encephalopathy, platelet dysfunction), hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, volume overload, hypertension, anemia, and renal osteodystrophy.
UR-12-A.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: chronic kidney disease, azotemia/uremic syndrome

UR-12-B.t: Explain ischemic and nephrotoxic acute tubular necrosis, with injury concentrated in the proximal tubule and thick ascending limb, tubular cell sloughing that obstructs flow, and muddy brown granular casts.
UR-12-B.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: tubulointerstitial disease: acute tubular necrosis

UR-12-B.t: Describe the initiation, maintenance (oliguria, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, volume overload), and recovery (polyuria with potassium and sodium loss) phases of acute tubular necrosis.
UR-12-B.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: tubulointerstitial disease: acute tubular necrosis

UR-12-B.t: Identify nephrotoxic causes of tubular necrosis (myoglobin from rhabdomyolysis, hemoglobin, aminoglycosides, iodinated contrast, cisplatin, ethylene glycol) and predict a dipstick positive for blood without RBCs on microscopy in rhabdomyolysis.
UR-12-B.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: tubulointerstitial disease: acute tubular necrosis

UR-12-B.t: Describe Fanconi syndrome as generalized proximal tubule dysfunction with glucosuria despite normal plasma glucose, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, and bicarbonaturia (proximal renal tubular acidosis), and identify causes such as cystinosis, Wilson disease, and multiple myeloma.
UR-12-B.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: Fanconi syndrome

UR-12-C.t: Identify causes of hydronephrosis by age and sex (posterior urethral valves, ureteropelvic junction obstruction, calculi, pregnancy, prostatic enlargement, pelvic tumors), and explain how persistent obstruction lowers GFR and causes papillary and cortical atrophy.
UR-12-C.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: obstructive uropathy

UR-12-C.t: Predict that unilateral hydronephrosis may stay silent while bilateral obstruction causes postrenal acute kidney injury with oliguria or anuria, and explain postobstructive diuresis after relief.
UR-12-C.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: obstructive uropathy

UR-12-C.t: Classify kidney stones by composition and urine pH: calcium oxalate (most common, hypercalciuria), calcium phosphate (alkaline urine), struvite (urease-producing bacteria, staghorn), uric acid (acidic urine, radiolucent, gout, tumor lysis), and cystine (hexagonal crystals).
UR-12-C.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: renal and ureteral calculi

UR-12-C.t: Describe renal colic (colicky flank pain radiating to the groin with hematuria) and the complications of calculi, including obstruction, hydronephrosis, and infection above the stone.
UR-12-C.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: renal and ureteral calculi

UR-12-D.t: Describe drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis as a hypersensitivity reaction days to weeks after drugs such as penicillins, NSAIDs, proton pump inhibitors, and diuretics, presenting with fever, rash, eosinophilia, pyuria with WBC casts, and rising creatinine.
UR-12-D.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: tubulointerstitial disease: acute interstitial nephritis

UR-12-D.t: Explain chronic analgesic nephropathy, with long-term combination analgesic use causing chronic interstitial nephritis and papillary necrosis, and identify other causes of papillary necrosis (diabetes, sickle cell disease, severe pyelonephritis, obstruction).
UR-12-D.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: tubulointerstitial disease: papillary necrosis

UR-12-D.t: Explain how vesicoureteral reflux or obstruction leads to chronic pyelonephritis, with coarse asymmetric corticomedullary scars over blunted calyces and thyroidization of tubules filled with eosinophilic casts.
UR-12-D.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: upper urinary tract: pyelonephritis

UR-12-D.t: Describe xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis as a chronic destructive infection, usually with obstructing stones and Proteus, filled with lipid-laden foamy macrophages that can mimic renal cell carcinoma.
UR-12-D.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: upper urinary tract: granulomatous pyelonephritis

UR-12-D.t: Describe interstitial cystitis (bladder pain syndrome) as chronic pelvic pain with urgency and frequency in the absence of infection, most often in women, with Hunner ulcers in some patients.
UR-12-D.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: interstitial cystitis

UR-12-E.t: Describe Alport syndrome: hematuria progressing to renal failure, sensorineural hearing loss, and anterior lenticonus, with thinning and splitting (basket-weave) of the glomerular basement membrane on electron microscopy, and more severe disease in males with X-linked inheritance.
UR-12-E.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: glomerular disease: Alport syndrome

UR-12-E.t: Describe autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in adults: bilaterally enlarged cystic kidneys, flank pain, hematuria, hypertension, progressive renal failure, hepatic cysts, berry aneurysms with subarachnoid hemorrhage, and mitral valve prolapse.
UR-12-E.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: benign neoplasms and cysts: polycystic kidney disease

UR-12-E.t: Distinguish autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (bilateral enlarged kidneys in infancy, Potter sequence, congenital hepatic fibrosis with portal hypertension) from multicystic dysplastic kidney (usually unilateral, noninherited) and acquired cystic disease in long-term dialysis (renal carcinoma risk).
UR-12-E.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Congenital disorders: renal dysplasia

UR-12-E.t: Explain how bilateral renal agenesis causes oligohydramnios and Potter sequence (pulmonary hypoplasia, flattened facies, limb deformities), while unilateral agenesis or a single kidney leads to compensatory hypertrophy of the other kidney.
UR-12-E.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Congenital disorders: renal agenesis, single kidney

UR-12-E.t: Explain how a short intravesical ureteral segment causes primary vesicoureteral reflux, predict recurrent pyelonephritis and reflux nephropathy scarring, and identify the voiding cystourethrogram as the diagnostic study.
UR-12-E.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: vesicoureteral reflux

UR-12-F.t: Explain how Shiga toxin from enterohemorrhagic E. coli O157:H7 damages endothelium in hemolytic uremic syndrome, causing microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with schistocytes, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury after bloody diarrhea in children, and contrast TTP (ADAMTS13 deficiency).

Distinguish benign nephrosclerosis (hyaline arteriolosclerosis, symmetrically shrunken kidneys with finely granular surfaces) from malignant hypertension (hyperplastic onion-skin arteriolosclerosis, fibrinoid necrosis, flea-bitten kidney, acute renal failure).
UR-12-F.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Metabolic and regulatory disorders: hypertensive renal disease

UR-12-F.t: Distinguish atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis (older adults, ostial or proximal lesion) from fibromuscular dysplasia (young women, string of beads), and explain renin-driven hypertension, an abdominal bruit, and atrophy of the affected kidney.
UR-12-F.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Vascular disorders: renal artery stenosis

UR-12-F.t: Describe renal infarction from emboli (atrial fibrillation, mural thrombus, endocarditis) or arterial thrombosis, producing a pale wedge-shaped coagulative infarct with flank pain and hematuria.
UR-12-F.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Vascular disorders: renal infarction

UR-12-F.t: Explain how the hypoxic, hypertonic, acidic renal medulla promotes sickling in the vasa recta, and predict isosthenuria, hematuria, and papillary necrosis in sickle cell disease and sickle cell trait.

Identify causes of renal vein thrombosis (nephrotic syndrome, especially membranous nephropathy; renal cell carcinoma invading the vein; dehydration in infants) and predict flank pain, hematuria, and an enlarged kidney.
UR-12-F.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Vascular disorders: renal vein thrombosis

UR-12-G.t: Describe clear cell renal cell carcinoma: proximal tubule origin, golden-yellow cut surface, lipid- and glycogen-filled clear cells, risk factors (smoking, obesity, hypertension, acquired cystic disease), and spread into the renal vein and inferior vena cava.
UR-12-G.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms: renal cell carcinoma

UR-12-G.t: Predict renal cell carcinoma presentations: hematuria, flank pain, and a flank mass, plus paraneoplastic polycythemia (erythropoietin), hypercalcemia (PTHrP), and hypertension (renin), and hematogenous spread to lung and bone.
UR-12-G.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms: renal cell carcinoma

UR-12-G.t: Distinguish papillary renal cell carcinoma (trisomy 7 and 17, papillae with foamy macrophages) and chromophobe carcinoma (intercalated cell origin) from clear cell carcinoma, and identify oncocytoma as a benign mitochondria-rich tumor.
UR-12-G.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms: renal cell carcinoma

UR-12-G.t: Describe Wilms tumor in children aged 2 to 5 years: a large unilateral flank mass, often with hematuria or hypertension, triphasic histology (blastema, stroma, epithelium), and associated syndromes (WAGR, Denys-Drash, Beckwith-Wiedemann).
UR-12-G.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms: Wilms tumor

UR-12-G.t: Describe urothelial carcinoma of the bladder and collecting system: painless hematuria, multifocal recurrence, flat carcinoma in situ versus papillary tumors, and risk factors (smoking, aromatic amine dyes, cyclophosphamide, phenacetin).
UR-12-G.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms: urinary bladder and collecting system

UR-12-G.t: Relate bladder squamous cell carcinoma to Schistosoma haematobium infection and chronic irritation, and bladder adenocarcinoma to urachal remnants and bladder exstrophy.
UR-12-G.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms: urinary bladder and collecting system

UR-12-H.t: Describe acute pyelonephritis: mostly ascending infection, fever, flank pain, costovertebral angle tenderness, WBC casts, and neutrophilic infiltration of the interstitium and tubules, with complications of papillary necrosis, perinephric abscess, pyonephrosis, and sepsis.
UR-12-H.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: upper urinary tract: pyelonephritis, perinephric and renal abscess, pyonephrosis

UR-12-H.t: Identify risk factors for cystitis (female sex, sexual intercourse, pregnancy, catheters, diabetes, obstruction) and distinguish cystitis (dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain, no fever) from pyelonephritis.
UR-12-H.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: lower urinary tract: cystitis

UR-12-H.t: Distinguish gonococcal urethritis (purulent discharge, gram-negative intracellular diplococci) from nongonococcal urethritis (Chlamydia trachomatis, scant discharge), and predict complications such as epididymitis, pelvic inflammatory disease, and reactive arthritis.
UR-12-H.usmle: Renal & Urinary System: Infectious disorders: lower urinary tract: chlamydial and nonchlamydial
